directAnswer: Use iCloud Backup for a hands-off wireless backup, or a computer (Finder on Mac / Apple Devices on Windows) for a full local backup you control.
summary: iCloud is easiest; a computer backup is better before major upgrades or repairs because you can keep an encrypted copy with passwords and Health data.

sections.heading: iCloud Backup
sections.body: Settings → [Your Name] → iCloud → iCloud Backup → Back Up Now. The iPhone must be locked, charging, and on Wi‑Fi. Check the timestamp after it finishes.

sections.heading: Computer backup
sections.body: Connect the iPhone, open Finder (macOS) or Apple Devices/iTunes (Windows), select the device, choose Back Up Now, and enable Encrypt local backup if you want passwords, Wi‑Fi settings, and Health data included.

steps.title: Confirm free space
steps.detail: iCloud backups fail silently when the plan is full — check iCloud storage first.

steps.title: Verify the latest backup date
steps.detail: Settings → [Your Name] → iCloud → iCloud Backup shows Last Successful Backup.

faqs.question: Does iCloud Backup include photos?
faqs.answer: If iCloud Photos is on, photos live in iCloud Photos and are not duplicated inside the device backup the same way. Keep both in mind when restoring.
